newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET CONTINUES FLUSH, RATES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET CONTINUES FLUSH, RATES MIXED.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened in excess of Z$1.2 billion on Wednesday on the back of maturing treasury bills with short-term trading rates mixed, dealers said.
"The market is quite liquid and the Reserve Bank indicated a surplus of Z$1.2 billion. This is due to treasury bills which are maturing and we had huge maturities yesterday," one dealer said.
He said discount houses were buying central bank paper at 18.90 percent and selling it in the market at 18.35 percent compared to 18.25 percent overnight.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 19.25 percent from 20 percent on Tuesday and selling at 19 percent versus 18.5 percent.

Bankers' acceptance bills were indicated at 19.25 percent (buying) and 18.75 percent (selling) compared to 19.5 percent and 18.5 percent (buying and selling respectively) while call money was quoted in an 18-18.50 percent range, versus 18 percent.
